title: Cookie-based session authentication with client-side expiry handling
context: The blueprint scope is public plus authenticated surfaces with session-based auth. The authentication model is a whole-project decision: the client, the API, and the deploy target must hold the same answer. A application-api-rest blueprint contributes its own decision on this topic; composition surfaces the pairing for operator reconciliation, which is intended.
decision: Authentication is a server-issued session carried in a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookie; the bundle never stores tokens in script-readable storage. The client treats 401 as session expiry: the current route is remembered, the session-expired surface renders, and successful re-authentication returns the user to the remembered route (application-spa-REQ-009). Sign-out invalidates server-side and clears client caches.
consequences: XSS cannot exfiltrate a bearer token because none is script-visible. CSRF posture must be handled with the API (SameSite plus the API blueprint auth classes). Session lifetime is server-owned; the client responds to expiry rather than predicting it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Bearer tokens in localStorage
alternativesConsidered.summary: JWT held by the client and attached per request.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Script-readable credentials fail the application-spa-REQ-018 floor.

alternativesConsidered.name: OAuth authorization-code with PKCE per session
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Valid where an external IdP is a project requirement; heavier than the blueprint default. Projects override by superseding this ADR.
